A.explanation: The arrows do not join head-to-tail in one continuous sense, so the resultant is not zero and equilibrium is not represented.

B.explanation: The left-side arrow points down the slope instead of up, so the loop does not close and the friction direction is reversed.

C.explanation: The vertical down weight, the normal perpendicular to the slope and the friction up the slope join head-to-tail in a closed loop for zero resultant.

D.explanation: The long vertical arrow points up, but weight must act vertically down, so this cannot be the correct force triangle.

hints: List the three forces on the block: weight vertically down, normal reaction perpendicular to the slope surface, and friction parallel to the slope up the slope.
For equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so when the three force vectors are placed head-to-tail they must form a closed triangle with all arrows pointing the same way round.
Check each triangle for the long vertical down arrow and then see which top and sloping sides continue head-to-tail back to the start without any arrow reversed.
walkthrough: Identify the forces: weight $W$ vertically down, normal force $N$ perpendicular to the slope and tilted to the left of vertical, and friction $F$ parallel to the slope acting up the slope to the right.
For equilibrium of coplanar forces, $W + N + F = 0$ as vectors, so the three vectors placed head-to-tail must form a closed triangle.
The longest side must therefore be the vertical arrow pointing down for $W$, which is present in A, B and C but reversed to up in D.
Starting at the tail of $W$ at the top, go down $W$ to the bottom vertex, then the next vector must start from that bottom tip.
Only a left-side arrow pointing up back toward the left vertex, followed by a top arrow pointing right back to the start, gives a continuous $L \to T \to B \to L$ loop.
In A and B one of the slope-force arrows points the wrong way, breaking the head-to-tail sequence, while D also reverses the weight.
This closed clockwise loop with correct relative orientations is shown in the diagram labelled C. This is option C
